rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes an APS AlCoCrFeNi coating on Q235 steel followed by furnace annealing, while the target used the same coating method and material on SS316L with annealing at 550 °C. The intervention type (APS coating + annealing) matches, but the substrate and specific annealing temperature differ.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions salt spray/humidity chambers at room temperature and ~100 °C, whereas the target used 3.5 wt% H2SO4 electrochemical testing and 900 °C cyclic hot corrosion with specific salt mixtures. The regimes are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis posits a passivation layer at the coating/substrate interface hindering diffusion, while the target's mechanism involves grain refinement, BCC phase, and Al/Cr-rich passive oxides on the coating surface resisting pit/crack development and molten salt attack. The general class (protective layer formation) is similar, but the specific pathway and location differ.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced corrosion rates and delayed degradation for coated/annealed Q235 versus untreated Q235. The target predicted and reported higher hardness, better electrochemical resistance, and lower hot-corrosion weight gain for coated/annealed SS316L versus uncoated and as-sprayed baselines. The property (corrosion resistance) and direction (improvement) align generally, but specifics differ.
